content:
Many people have complained in recent years that Apple's designs have lost some of their signature whimsy. Well, here's the latest sign that the tide may be turning.

Hidden inside the Settings app in iOS 27 is an Easter egg paying homage to a classic Mac OS character: Clarus the Dogcow. Here's how to trigger it...

iOS 27 adds a new feature that lets users customise the intensity of the Liquid Glass transparency effect via a slider that goes from "Clear" to "Tinted". You can find this option on your iPhone by going to Settings -> Appearance -> Liquid Glass.

On this page, Apple has included a mock website interface so you can preview how the Liquid Glass appearance changes as you adjust the slider. It contains a scrollable area featuring text and photos of Apple Park.

Here's the Easter egg: scroll all the way to the bottom, then keep swiping up with your finger, and an image of a Clarus the Dogcow figurine will appear, right next to the pond at Apple Park. And in the demo's search text field, rainbow-coloured text reading "Moof!" (the sound a dogcow makes) will also appear.

On top of that, if you type "Moof!" to Siri via Spotlight, Siri will reply, "Nice dogcow."

For those unfamiliar with the history, Clarus the Dogcow dates back to an icon created by Susan Kare for the original Mac, as a character in the Cairo font (the classic Mac's icon font, similar to Windows' Dingbats). The icon had essentially no practical use — it was purely for fun.
